courses.title: Barrio Organization and Service Learning
courses.description: Seminar, two hours; discussion, two hours; field placement, six hours. Limited to juniors/seniors. Service learning placement in community-based organization, labor union, or service-oriented nonprofit organization. Study of role that these organizations play in improvement and change of Chicana/Chicano communities. courses.title: Immigration and Chicano Community
courses.description: Lecture, three hours. Discussion on relationship between international immigration and development of Chicana/Chicano community. Examination of U.S. immigration policy and relationship between Mexican-origin population and other Latin American immigrants. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.title: Barrio Popular Culture
courses.description: Lecture, three hours. Construction of model by which to organize study of Chicana/Chicano popular culture by focusing on barrio as metaphor for community. courses.title: Gendered Politics and Chicana/Latina Political Participation
courses.description: Lecture, four hours. Examination of Chicanas and Latinas as participants, organizers, and leaders in communities, workplaces, labor unions, and government. Survey of Chicanas/Latinas in politics and as policymakers in appointed and elected offices. Analysis of gendering of politics and political behavior. Letter grading.

courses.title: History of Chicana/Chicano Los Angeles, 20th Century
courses.description: Lecture, four hours. History of Mexican American people in 20th-century Los Angeles. Readings and lectures emphasize formation of regional identity among Mexican Americans in Los Angeles and their significance to emergence of multicultural metropolis. Letter grading.

courses.title: Health in Chicano/Latino Population
courses.description: (Same as Public Health M106.) Lecture, four hours; discussion, one hour. Designed for juniors/seniors. Examination of Chicano/Latino health status through life expectancy, causes of death, reportable diseases, services utilization, provider supply, and risk behaviors within demographic/immigration changes. courses.title: Chicano/Latino Community Formation: Critical Perspectives and Oral Histories
courses.description: (Same as Labor Studies M123.) Lecture, four hours. Analysis of historical formation and development of Chicano/Latino communities in 20th century, with focus on labor, immigration, economic structures, electoral politics, and international dimensions. Letter grading.

courses.title: Issues in Latina/Latino Poverty: Mexican and Central American Voices from Los Angeles
courses.description: (Same as Labor Studies M121 and Urban Planning M140.) Lecture, four hours. Examination of key issues (work, housing, and neighborhoods) in urban poverty, with particular focus on Mexican and Central American immigrant populations in Los Angeles. courses.title: Planning Issues in Latina/Latino Communities: Preserving and Strengthening Community Assets in Mexican and Salvadoran Los Angeles
courses.description: (Same as Labor Studies M122 and Urban Planning M171.) Lecture, four hours. How community and economic development interact, role of assets in community development, and unique synergies and pitfalls that enable or disable communities from developing to their potential. courses.title: Women's Movement in Latin America
courses.description: (Same as Gender Studies M144 and Labor Studies M144.) Lecture, four hours. courses.title: Introduction to Study of Spanish Grammar: Phonology and Morphology
courses.description: Lecture, four hours. Requisite: course M35. Analysis of phonemic and morphological systems of Spanish. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.title: Introduction to Study of Spanish Grammar: Syntax
courses.description: Lecture, four hours. Requisite: course M35. Study of syntactical systems of Spanish. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.title: Introduction to Literary Analysis
courses.description: Lecture, four hours. Requisite: course 25 or 27. Introduction to methods of analyzing literary work in Spanish, Spanish-American, and Chicana/Chicano literature. Special attention to four major genres: poetry, narrative, drama, and essay. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.title: Advanced Spanish Composition
courses.description: Lecture, three hours. Requisite: course 5. Emphasis on development of communicative abilities, both verbal and written, as well as on increasing comprehension of variety of forms of cultural production in Spanish language and on preparation for more advanced Spanish courses. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.title: Advanced Spanish Composition for Heritage Speakers
courses.description: Lecture, three hours. Requisite: course 7B or equivalent. Not open for credit to students with credit for course 25. Practice in reading and writing of Spanish for students with oral proficiency in Spanish (in lieu of course 25). P/NP or letter grading.

courses.title: Iberian Cultures
courses.description: Lecture, four hours; discussion, one hour. Required of majors. Lectures taught in English; discussion sections taught in either Spanish or English. Highlights of civilization of Spain, with emphasis on artistic, economic, social, and historical development as background for upper-division courses. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.title: Latin American Cultures
courses.description: Lecture, four hours; discussion, one hour. Required of majors. Lectures taught in English; discussion sections taught in either Spanish or English. Highlights of civilization of Spanish America, with emphasis on artistic, economic, social, and historical development as background for upper-division courses. P/NP or letter grading.
